sourceInformation.genre: Anti-gravity combat racing (arcade), with survival and combat-points modes
sourceInformation.perspective: Third-person chase camera (near, far, cockpit) with trackside TV cameras
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge engine v0.85.2 and its 3D add-on, three.js r182 (WebGPU renderer with WebGL 2 fallback), Rapier 0.19.3 (loaded by the add-on, unused by craft), AI Hub session client 1.4.0, plain JavaScript
sourceInformation.artDirection: The engine native pixel-resolution 3D look: low-resolution vertex-coloured meshes, flat light, neon glow with bloom, pixel HUD and fonts
sourceInformation.animation: Engine fixed-step loop; craft tilt, roll, banking and camera swing driven by physics values; no keyframes
sourceInformation.audio: All synthesized in code with the engine chip synth: layered songs per track, engine hum, sound effects, Animalese-style gibberish voice. No audio files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub ghost-race session (mode ghost, 1 to 4 players) through the vendored hub client; on its own the game has local 2-player split-screen VERSUS
sourceInformation.testing: Headless tests behind one command (node tests/run.mjs --browser): Node simulation suites with bot players, plus a Playwright Chromium suite on the bundled file that plays every mode, drives the game with a stubbed DualSense and the keyboard, runs attract and a stand-in AI Hub; screenshots only for layout; no subagents
sourceInformation.research: None beyond PLAN.md, the engine docs and the AI Hub client
sourceInformation.environment: Claude Code CLI (headless); Linux; browser unknown

testingFeedback: Eleven real issues: a syntax error that blocked boot, E.World3D.INPUT read before the 3D add-on loads, craft launched 140 m into the air by a vertical-speed bug, spurious take-offs from slice-edge noise, double lap time on finishing, scratch-frame aliasing in the track queries, Math.random leaking into the sim (found by the replay-hash test), weapons far too lethal for a human, an Academy drill that could soft-lock, a missing font glyph, and keyboard X and B drawn as Xbox buttons.
Three: the boot-blocking syntax error, the craft launching into the sky, and the Academy weapon drill that could never complete once a weapon was held.

The Node bot suite: a bot drives every track and class, plus full-grid races whose seeded hash must repeat. It found the sky-launch, the nondeterminism and the lethal weapon balance without anyone looking at a picture.
The per-weapon fires-once checks: they never failed. Screenshots of menus were also low value apart from the missing glyph and the glyph-chip bug.
engineFeedback: The fixed-step loop with game.advance, so whole races, the attract timer and a stand-in hub could be played headless in seconds; the standard pause, settings, rebinding and boot screens; the chip synth with layers; and World3D taking plain three.js meshes in node materials with bloom and the pixel look for free.

Yes. E.World3D does not exist when classic scripts run (the add-on is a deferred module), so E.World3D.INPUT crashed at boot. game.advance right after game.go does not switch scenes until a real frame has passed. audio.sfx has no delay option, so the gibberish voice uses timers.
Track-space hover physics on banked splines with crest air time, the track, craft and scenery mesh builders, the ten weapons and the AI, and the 10-foot menu and glyph kit.

Using World3D as a pure renderer: it wants a level or terrain, so a one-tile pit level stands in; the engine axes (x east, y south, z up) map to three.js with a reflection, which made winding and camera roll signs a matter of trial and error; and the picture could only be checked by screenshots.
One small thing: the button-symbol setting defaults to PlayStation, sits under Display, and offers PlayStation or Xbox. Marked SNIPEOUT EDIT in engine/my-3d2dge.js.
Make E.World3D.INPUT and E.World3D.SETTINGS available before the add-on loads (or load it synchronously), and add a levelless mode for worlds made only of custom meshes.
promptFeedback: The plan: pinned versions, axis and unit conventions, the determinism rules, the hub skeleton and the one-command testing rule saved hours and kept the build coherent.

The scale. The plan lists four tracks, six songs, split-screen VERSUS, replays, tunnels, gap jumps and eleven drills; all of it is built, and some plan paths use another run folder name than TASK.md (TASK.md won).
Keeping every feature complete with no stubs across that much content, and testing the controller and the hub without real hardware, using a stubbed gamepad and a stand-in hub.
Mark which plan features are mandatory and which may be cut, shorten the plan, and say whether a plan-driven build may drop plan-only features.

aiHub.name: SNIPEOUT HD
aiHub.description: An anti-gravity combat racer inspired by Wipeout HD: banked roller-coaster tracks, ten weapons, airbrakes and a deadpan league that sponsors everything. Race, snipe, survive Overclock, play 2-player split screen or race ghosts of other players in a hub session.
aiHub.controls: Steer A/D or left stick, thrust W or ✕, airbrakes Q/E or L2/R2, fire Space or □, absorb F or ○
